paragraphs: On Thursday, Teacher Kim showed a short film in the library during the club hour. It was called "The Little Boat," and it was twelve minutes long. The boy in the film was born in a village on the coast. He wanted to take people across the water in a small boat. An old man told him, "You need a license, and you are too young." The boy waited, and he helped his mother serve fish soup in the village shop. Every morning, he looked at the boat and the water.

When the film ended, Teacher Kim asked, "What is your opinion?" "Please give a reason for your opinion." "I liked the film," said Mia, "because the boy did not stop." "He waited a long time, and he did not stop." "I agree," said May, "and I especially liked the music." "It was slow and quiet, like the water."

"I did not like the middle," said Leo. "It was too slow, and nothing happened." "I do not agree," said Lily. "A lot of things happened, but the film showed them in small ways." "For example, the boy helped his mother immediately when a customer came." "That showed that he was kind." "Maybe," said Leo, "but I still think it was slow." "Which part did you like, Leo?" asked Mia. "I liked the end, because the boat moved fast on the water," said Leo.

"What is your opinion about the license rule?" asked Teacher Kim. "I think the rule is fair," said May. "A boat can be dangerous, so a driver needs a license." "I think it is too hard for the boy," said Leo. "He knew the water very well, and he was born on the coast." "But a license shows that you are able to drive well," said Lily. "I agree with May," said Mia. "The rule is for everybody, and it keeps people safe."

Teacher Kim smiled and looked at the four friends. "I like your opinions, because every one has a reason," she said. "You do not need to agree with each other." "Next week, you can choose the film." Lily opened her notebook and wrote a title for the blog. The title was, "Our Opinions About The Little Boat." Leo laughed and said, "Please write that Leo wants a faster film next time."

sentences.text: On Thursday, Teacher Kim showed a short film in the library during the club hour.
It was called "The Little Boat," and it was twelve minutes long.
The boy in the film was born in a village on the coast.
He wanted to take people across the water in a small boat.
An old man told him, "You need a license, and you are too young."
The boy waited, and he helped his mother serve fish soup in the village shop.
Every morning, he looked at the boat and the water.
When the film ended, Teacher Kim asked, "What is your opinion?"
"Please give a reason for your opinion."
"I liked the film," said Mia, "because the boy did not stop."
"He waited a long time, and he did not stop."
"I agree," said May, "and I especially liked the music."
"It was slow and quiet, like the water."
"I did not like the middle," said Leo.
"It was too slow, and nothing happened."
"I do not agree," said Lily.
"A lot of things happened, but the film showed them in small ways."
"For example, the boy helped his mother immediately when a customer came."
"That showed that he was kind."
"Maybe," said Leo, "but I still think it was slow."
"Which part did you like, Leo?" asked Mia.
"I liked the end, because the boat moved fast on the water," said Leo.
"What is your opinion about the license rule?" asked Teacher Kim.
"I think the rule is fair," said May.
"A boat can be dangerous, so a driver needs a license."
"I think it is too hard for the boy," said Leo.
"He knew the water very well, and he was born on the coast."
"But a license shows that you are able to drive well," said Lily.
"I agree with May," said Mia.
"The rule is for everybody, and it keeps people safe."
Teacher Kim smiled and looked at the four friends.
"I like your opinions, because every one has a reason," she said.
"You do not need to agree with each other."
"Next week, you can choose the film."
Lily opened her notebook and wrote a title for the blog.
The title was, "Our Opinions About The Little Boat."
Leo laughed and said, "Please write that Leo wants a faster film next time."
